subject: geography
title: How Rivers Shape the Land
welcome_lead: Follow the flow! Rivers carve valleys, carry rocks and build new land. Discover how erosion shapes everything from streams to mighty rivers.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on river erosion processes including hydraulic action and abrasion.
final_note: Brilliant! You now know the main types of river erosion.

concepts.def: Wearing away of land by water, wind or ice.
Force of water hitting and breaking rocks.
Rocks scraping against riverbed and banks.
Water dissolving soluble rocks like limestone.

walkthroughs.h2: Four ways rivers wear away the land
walkthroughs.body_html:
• Hydraulic action: water force breaks rocks.
  • Abrasion: stones scrape the bed.
  • Attrition: stones knock and shrink.
  • Solution: water dissolves rock.
Near the source, rivers flow fast down steep slopes. Vertical erosion creates V-shaped valleys and waterfalls.
Near the mouth, the river is wide and slow. It deposits sediment, forming floodplains and deltas.
